sourceReceipts.title: Anatomy of a Frontier Lab Agent Intrusion: A Technical Timeline of the July 2026 Incident

It reports five challenge-related datasets and limited operational metadata accessed, with no unauthorized supply-chain change shipped. This is affected-party primary evidence; remediation effectiveness remains unverified.

sourceReceipts.title: Training novices to think, or giving them LLMs? Evidence from an RCT
sourceReceipts.notes: The complete 49-page provider-affiliated working paper was read. In a preregistered 2x2 classroom RCT with 1,053 first-year students, GPT-4o improved performance on a tightly specified merchandising task while causal-reasoning training increased mechanism identification, falsifiability and idea diversity. The bounded task, classroom-level assignment, self-reported compliance, LLM-based measures and lack of peer review limit generalization.

sourceReceipts.title: Previewing the Model Hardware Standard

Safety evaluations are still being developed and the standard is not yet open source; setup-time and performance claims remain provider-reported.

Anthropic explicitly says safeguards cannot remove prompt-injection risk and advises against sensitive financial, medical or third-party personal-data actions. Availability and safety remain plan, platform, rollout and task specific.

sourceReceipts.title: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT

OpenAI tells users to verify sensitive steps and results because safeguards do not eliminate prompt injection, phishing or unintended-action risk.

sourceReceipts.title: Temporary Chat FAQ
sourceReceipts.notes: OpenAI now distinguishes non-personalized and personalized Temporary Chats. Personalized temporary chats may use existing memories, custom instructions and plugins but do not create new memories unless saved; unsaved temporary chats stay out of history and may be retained for up to 30 days for safety. This is a current product rule, not a general privacy guarantee, and account or workspace restrictions still apply.

sourceReceipts.title: AI agents can act. That's the security problem.

It does not implement production compliance policy or prove orchestration on its default offline path. The durable boundary pattern merges with existing permission and evidence work.

opportunities.title: Explain the changing system of skills for working with AI
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can recognize that effective AI work now spans context, memory, projects, reusable skills, agents, tools, permissions, loops and verification rather than treating prompt length as the whole practice.
opportunities.facts: AIDB published skills-map, advanced-user and assistant-to-operator episodes. OpenAI and Anthropic now document separate browser environments, signed-in-session boundaries, plan-specific availability, confirmation and prompt-injection limitations. OpenAI documents personalized Temporary Chats that may use existing context without creating new memories. Salesforce and Anthropic document a pilot that combines model reasoning with a system of record and business rules. Cursor and OpenAI show that a product's model access can change after ownership and contract changes.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: AIDB frames recent interface and harness changes as the practical move from assistant to operator. Salesforce and Anthropic argue that enterprise data, rules and workflows remain valuable around models. OpenAI frames its Cursor cutoff as contractual and safety accountability; Cursor frames its SpaceX acquisition as a path to stronger and cheaper models.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The useful unit is no longer a prompt in isolation. It is a task plus model, harness, context, memory, tools, external systems, permissions, stop conditions, verification and a human decision owner. Moving from suggestion to action makes access and accountability more important, while model access inside a product is contingent rather than permanent.

opportunities.title: Explain how AI changes the shape of work, not only the number of jobs
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can distinguish tasks, jobs and organizations, then see where context, tools, judgment, responsibility and decision rights move when agents take on more work.
opportunities.facts: AIDB's August 16, 23 and 25 editions examine work redesign and human-agent organizations. OpenAI's enterprise-customer report supplies an adoption pattern but not representative worker outcomes or direct evidence of value.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: AIDB argues that the job-loss question is too blunt and that leading organizations increasingly move from assistance to delegated systems-level work.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The new episode strengthens the existing theme and adds a useful measurement dispute: activity and output are not the same as value. LAiDIES should explain who designs the system, who reviews it, who gains, who bears failure and who retains decision rights.

opportunities.title: Teach agentic delegation through permissions, boundaries and review
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can understand why giving AI tools changes the job from writing a better prompt to deciding what to delegate, defining access, checking the result and owning the consequences.
opportunities.facts: Mollick and AIDB establish a delegation frame. OpenAI, METR and Hugging Face supply a reconciled incident record. OpenAI and Anthropic now document browser agents with separate sessions, permissions, confirmations and explicit residual prompt-injection risk. The evidence-grounded AML example separates deterministic evidence, model proposals, application controls and qualified-human authority.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: AIDB argues that browser and harness upgrades are moving assistants toward operators. OpenAI and Anthropic present product safeguards while warning that they cannot remove every risk. The Neuron interview argues that security must span data, tools, memory, permissions and continuous tests, but its extreme-risk language remains vendor interpretation.
opportunities.laidiesInference: Browser access turns a fluent answer into a consequential workflow. Good delegation requires least privilege, isolated or intentionally shared state, approved communications, safe stop conditions, evidence that validates claim support rather than citation syntax, active monitoring and a human who can halt and own the work.

opportunities.title: Explain why a spectacular AI benefit would not settle the trust question
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can separate whether AI delivers a benefit from who controls it, who can afford it, who bears the risk and who can challenge the terms.
opportunities.facts: AIDB published an August 17 long-form episode about AI-company promises and public trust; the complete edition and transcript were accessible.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: AIDB argues that trust cannot be repaired by messaging alone and that delivery matters, while also acknowledging that a breakthrough does not erase questions about access, price, opacity, lobbying, distribution or institutional power.
opportunities.laidiesInference: The strongest reader frame is not whether one promised breakthrough makes AI good or bad. It is how evidence of benefit interacts with governance, distribution and the public's ability to influence consequential systems.

opportunities.attributedInterpretation: Anthropic presents shared memory as a way to reduce re-explaining and carry project context between chat and Cowork while preserving user controls.

opportunities.title: Measure reasoning, not only polished output
opportunities.readerValue: Readers can see why a fluent answer may hide what a person understands, then learn to ask for mechanisms, failure conditions, originality and transfer as well as polish.
opportunities.facts: A provider-affiliated classroom RCT with 1,053 first-year students found that GPT-4o access improved scores on a tightly specified merchandising task while causal-reasoning training increased mechanism identification, falsifiability and idea diversity. The standard rubric did not reward those unconventional answers.
opportunities.attributedInterpretation: The authors argue that AI and causal-reasoning training can have complementary effects and that evaluation systems must demand diversity if they value it.
opportunities.laidiesInference: LAiDIES should not equate a polished final artifact with learning. Material teaching and internal evaluation should look for causal mechanism, limitations, explain-back, unseen transfer and review burden. One bounded study does not establish a universal education rule.
